A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PTDI and retain the same research problem and benchmarks despite retitling and substantial revision. All 24 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix F report original LLM/VLM experiments measuring FDR, power, and estimator bias and MSE.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix F report original experiments, including adaptive-method comparisons, FIR and power measurements, and JKBB estimator evaluation.

M1.justification: The subtraction estimator based on a calibration-score tail region in v1 Section 3.2 is replaced by the JKBB p-value boundary-density estimator in v2 Section 3.3. This introduces dual-bandwidth Beta kernels, jackknife correction, and bandwidth selection. The surrounding conformal-p-value/BH procedure and adjusted moment extension remain.

E1.justification: Both evaluate WikiMIA and ArXivTection for LLM pre-training, XSum and BBC Real Time for fine-tuning, and VL-MIA/Flickr and VL-MIA/DALL-E for VLMs. The input-component and membership-mixture scenarios are retained. Removing some ArXivTection tables does not remove that benchmark’s coverage.

E2.justification: V1 Table 1 compares the proposed scaling procedure only with Vanilla BH. V2 Table 1 additionally evaluates Storey-BH, BKY, and Quantile-BH across the retained WikiMIA models and scores. KTD and Vanilla remain evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 changes the LLaVA MaxRényi-K% setting from K=10 to K=100. Figure 5 changes the calibration-size study from NeoX/Pythia to LLaMA/NeoX configurations and reduces its target-level range. These are localized setting revisions; the main splitting procedure remains, and FIR is mathematically the same metric as v1’s FDR.

E4.justification: The selection-procedure ablation expands to adaptive BH alternatives, while the calibration-size analysis drops power curves and displays two detection scores. V1’s eta-sensitivity study and additional ArXivTection scaling ablation are removed. Estimator-accuracy and moment-versus-default analyses are revised for JKBB, substantially changing the ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain 1,000-run averaging and Figure 5’s mean-plus-or-minus-one-standard-deviation reporting. V2 Appendix C.5 additionally describes subsampling or bootstrapping to estimate means and normalized standard deviations for gamma selection. This adds a resampling-based uncertainty calculation, without establishing increased experimental run counts.

E6.justification: Table 1 reports substantially revised values: NeoX/MIN-K% at alpha=0.1 has Vanilla/Ours power of 5%/12% in v1 versus 1.69%/6.05% in v2. These are replaced results, not established comparable-setting gains: the proposed estimator changes and WikiMIA preprocessing is incompletely matched. Adaptive-baseline and JKBB bias/MSE results are added, while v1 Tables 4–6 are removed.

T1.justification: V1’s subtraction-estimator bound and finite-sample control theorem are replaced by asymptotic plug-in control arguments. V2 adds extensive JKBB bias, variance, bandwidth, consistency, and convergence-rate derivations, plus a power-dominance theorem and an explicit adjusted-moment control theorem. The FDR-to-FIR renaming itself does not change the mathematical error definition.

C1.justification: V1 explicitly claims distribution-free, finite-sample FDR control. V2 removes that finite-sample promise and centers its contribution on JKBB boundary consistency, with Theorem 3.1 providing asymptotic control. The existing confirmed-member extension is promoted into the contribution list rather than newly introduced.

C2.justification: V2 explains power through correcting Storey-style boundary-estimation bias and interprets estimator results through accuracy rather than v1’s uniformly negative-bias conservatism. Appendix D removes the heuristic finite-sample assurance for the moment correction. The distribution-matching limitation remains, with a new suggestion to investigate weighted conformal p-values.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset and split counts in Table 3, adaptive-baseline implementation rules in Appendix E.2, and practical bandwidth and gamma-selection details in Appendix C, including the penalty default lambda=1. These materially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v1’s explicit 32-token WikiMIA preprocessing disclosure disappears without a replacement setting.

R1.justification: The central positioning shifts from overcoming KTD and conservative conformal selection to improving adaptive BH null-proportion estimation. Appendix A substantially expands discussion of Storey-BH, BKY, Quantile-BH, and boundary bias, with new references including Storey, Chen, Neuvial, and Schucany–Sommers. Jin–Candès remains cited despite removal of its earlier detailed comparison.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, introduction, contributions, method narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Problem formulation moves from the preliminaries into the method section, detection-score explanations are reorganized, and the appendices are restructured. FDR/FDP terminology changes throughout to FIR/FIP.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, restructures Table 1, and adds a dataset-count table. Figure 3 becomes a single GPT-2 plot, Figure 5 becomes error-only panels, and v1 Tables 4–6 and Figure 8 disappear. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The adaptive baselines and implementation details strengthen comparison and reproducibility. However, the replacement theory has inconsistent kernel definitions in Equations 11 and 22 and an unjustified FIP-monotonicity step in Proposition B.3. Detailed error-control tables are removed, and Figure 3’s WikiMIA caption conflicts with the BBC Real Time discussion. These issues affect the revised method’s central evidential reliability, so the benefits do not establish a confident net improvement over v1.
